content: 1. The 1997 study published in Sexuality and Disability explored various aspects of sexuality in individuals with disabilities, providing insights into their unique challenges and needs. 2. The Voluntary HIV-1 Counseling and Testing Efficacy Study Group conducted a randomized trial in Kenya, Tanzania, and Trinidad, published in The Lancet in 2000, which demonstrated the effectiveness of voluntary HIV-1 counseling and testing for individuals and couples in reducing HIV transmission. 3. Thrun et al. (2009) reported on the Positive STEPs intervention, a multisite, clinic-based program that improved HIV prevention counseling by care providers, as published in AIDS Education and Prevention. 4. Troussier (2011) discussed risk behaviors among adolescent girls in a French publication, Réalité en Gynécologie Obstétrique, emphasizing the importance of addressing these behaviors in gynecological and obstetric care. 5. Troussier and Tourette-Turgis (2006) highlighted how improving the quality of sexual and emotional life can enhance prevention efforts among individuals living with HIV, as published in the Revue Européenne de Sexologie. 6. Troussier, Benghozi, and Ganem (2012) examined high-risk sexual behaviors in the context of pediatric adrenal disease, as part of an evidence-based clinical practice guide edited by Sultan and published by Karger. 7. Turner et al. (1998) demonstrated that the use of computer survey technology increased reporting of adolescent sexual behavior, drug use, and violence, as published in Science. 8. Van Reeuwijk and Nahar (2013) emphasized the importance of adopting a positive approach to sexuality in sexual health programs for unmarried adolescents in Bangladesh, as detailed in Reproductive Health Matters. 9. Villaroman-Bautista et al. (1990) compared the use patterns, healthcare processes, and effectiveness of four prenatal health services in a provincial community in the Philippines, as reported in the Maternal Nutrition and Health Care Program Report. 10. Vlassoff and Fonn (2001) described the Health Workers for Change initiative as a tool for health systems management and development, as published in Health Policy and Planning. 11. Walker and Harrington (2002) evaluated the effects of staff training on knowledge and attitudes about sexuality in Educational Gerontology, showing significant improvements in these areas. 12. Warner et al. (2008) assessed the impact of a brief video intervention on reducing incident infections among patients attending sexually transmitted disease clinics, as published in PLoS Medicine. 13. Welbourn (1995) developed the Stepping Stones training package, which focuses on HIV/AIDS, communication, and relationship skills, published by Strategies for Hope in London. 14. Wenger et al. (1992) conducted a randomized clinical trial that demonstrated a reduction in high-risk sexual behavior among heterosexual individuals undergoing HIV antibody testing, as published in the American Journal of Public Health. 15. The WHO Handbook for Guideline Development (2012) provided a comprehensive framework for evidence-based guideline creation, accessible through the World Health Organization. 16. Young et al. (2002) investigated the prevalence of abuse among women with physical disabilities, as published in Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation. 17. Baldwin (2001) explored the relationship between depression and sexual dysfunction in a detailed review published in the British Medical Bulletin. 18. Boekeloo et al. (1999) conducted a trial on STD/HIV prevention among adolescents in managed care, as reported in Pediatrics. 19. Bowman et al. (1992) examined the impact of educational preparation on physician performance with simulated patients presenting sexually transmitted diseases, as published in Archives of Internal Medicine. 20. Carey et al. (2010) evaluated the effectiveness of brief and intensive behavioral interventions to promote sexual risk reduction among STD clinic patients, as published in AIDS Behavior. 21. Cohen et al. (1992) reported on the outcomes of brief condom promotion programs, highlighting their effectiveness for men but not women, as published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. 22. Dodge et al. (2001) described a comprehensive clinical intervention to enhance primary care HIV prevention, as published in the American Journal of Preventive Medicine. 23. Feldblum et al. (2005) conducted a randomized trial on male condom promotion among sex workers in Madagascar, as published in Sexually Transmitted Infections. 24. Jemmott et al. (2007) evaluated the effects of brief HIV/STI prevention interventions on sexual risk behavior and STI rates among African American women in primary care settings, as published in the American Journal of Public Health. 25. Kamb et al. (1998) demonstrated the efficacy of risk-reduction counseling in preventing HIV and sexually transmitted diseases in a randomized controlled trial, as part of the Project RESPECT Study Group, published in JAMA. 26. Marrazzo et al. (2011) investigated a behavioral intervention to reduce bacterial vaginosis persistence among women who have sex with women, as published in Sexually Transmitted Infections. 27. Neumann et al. (2011) assessed the effectiveness of the VOICES/VOCES intervention for STD/HIV prevention when implemented by health department staff, as published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. 28. Patterson et al. (2008) evaluated a brief behavioral intervention to promote condom use among female sex workers in Tijuana and Ciudad Juarez, Mexico, as published in the American Journal of Public Health. 29. Thrun et al. (2009) reported on the Positive STEPs intervention, which improved prevention counseling by HIV care providers in a multisite, clinic-based setting, as published in AIDS Education and Prevention. 30. Warner et al. (2008) demonstrated the effectiveness of a brief video intervention in reducing incident infections among patients attending sexually transmitted disease clinics, as published in PLoS Medicine.
